scenarios.name: favorable_free_cooling
scenarios.description: Normal OS#2: 10 °C outdoor air against a 13 °C setpoint. Even after the 1 °C fan rise the air arrives at 11 °C, so the damper has room to modulate and the changeover is correct.

scenarios.name: oat_well_above_setpoint
scenarios.description: 20 °C outdoor air against a 13 °C setpoint: the gap is 7 °C, far past the 1.0 °C threshold. Free cooling cannot reach setpoint at any damper position, so the alarm asserts once the 30 min delay expires.

scenarios.name: edge_gap_equals_threshold
scenarios.description: Strict boundary, clear side: oat − sat_sp = 1.0 °C exactly. GreaterThreshold is u > t, so sitting precisely on the composed epsilon budget is not a fault.

scenarios.name: edge_gap_just_over_threshold
scenarios.description: Strict boundary, fault side: oat − sat_sp = 1.1 °C clears u > t and alarms after the delay. Pins the same edge as edge_gap_equals_threshold from the other direction.

scenarios.name: fan_heat_narrows_the_band
scenarios.description: Teaching case for the sign of dTSF: a 1.5 °C gap faults because fan heat is subtracted from the epsilon budget (1 + 1 − 1 = 1.0). Had the threshold been sensor error alone (2.0 °C), this unit would read healthy while outdoor air 0.5 °C above setpoint gains another 1 °C crossing the fan.

scenarios.name: setpoint_drop_opens_the_gap
scenarios.description: Outdoor air holds at 13.5 °C while the SAT reset walks the setpoint from 14 °C down to 12 °C at t = 600 s. Nothing outdoors changed; the unit simply now demands colder supply air than free cooling can deliver. The delay runs from the setpoint step, so the alarm lands at 2400 s.

scenarios.name: transient_warm_spell_never_alarms
scenarios.description: A 1200 s excursion to 20 °C — shorter than the 1800 s alarm delay — then back to 10 °C. The persistence timer resets on the first compliant tick and nothing is reported.

scenarios.name: fault_clears_on_recovery
scenarios.description: Sustained 7 °C gap alarms at 1800 s; outdoor air falls back to 10 °C at 3600 s and the alarm drops on that tick. Recovery has no delay — only the assertion does.
